findings.title: Spec asserts middleware.redact_token_route covers /reference/* — no such arm exists; false assurance ships to rc3-3/rc3-4
findings.evidence: spec:158 "The token-redaction registry (`middleware.redact_token_route`) covers `/reference/*` server-side; the helpers must not add a second leak path." middleware.gleam:330-342: `fn redact_token_route(segments: List(String)) -> Result(String, Nil) { case segments { ["dsar", ..] -> ... ["erase", ..] -> ... ["apply", code, "resume", ..] -> ... ["apply", code, "draft-erasure", ..] -> ... _ -> Error(Nil) } }` — no ["reference", ..] arm.
findings.detail: The merged spec states a safety control that does not exist. No leak today (the /reference routes land in rc3-3/rc3-4), but those stories will trust this claim and may skip adding the arm, leaking referee capability tokens into Sentry event paths and access logs.
findings.recommended_fix: Correct the spec sentence to say the arm must be added when rc3-3/rc3-4 land the routes; add `["reference", ..] -> Ok("/reference/<redacted>")` to redact_token_route in the story that wires the router entries.

findings.title: Warm-handoff email deviates from pinned copy beyond the three documented deviations (extra sentence + parenthesised detail)
findings.evidence: "Their contact details and the same log are on the application page. If they complete the form anyway, it still shows up there." + `detail -> " (" <> email_client.escape_html(detail) <> ")"` vs spec pin: "Their contact details and the same log are on the application page." + one line per attempt `• {at}: {channel}, {outcome} {detail}`
findings.detail: The story contract is verbatim-minus-documented-deviations (enforced by pruning an extra co-nudge line for exactly this reason). The added sentence and the parens around attempt detail are neither in the three deviations nor in the dev record's delta list. Tests pin the implementation, not the spec.
findings.recommended_fix: Either revert to the pinned strings, or add both to the spec's deviations register and pin them with tests so the copy contract stays honest.

findings.title: AC3 email sender identity + template tags unobservable to the suite; send_reminder never exercised with ReminderTwo
findings.evidence: send.gleam:30 `const referee_sender: String = "RightTenantry References <references@righttenantry.ie>"` / :34 `const standard_sender ...` referenced only inside the non-empty-key branch (:194-203); every send_test case uses `no_key_deps()`; the only stage exercise is `send.send_reminder(no_key_deps(), messages.ReminderOne, fixture_message())` (ReminderTwo never passed). Grep over test/ for the sender consts and reference_* tags: no hits.
findings.detail: A typo in either sender, a swapped referee/applicant sender, or a wrong template tag would pass the suite green. The spec Verify clause demanded "send-helper tests assert the sms_client/email_client payload wiring" — only the no-op branches are pinned.
findings.recommended_fix: Expose a pure sender/tag selection (or build via the public email_client.build_send_body seam) and pin referee_sender vs standard_sender, the four reference_* tags, and ReminderTwo through send_reminder.

findings.title: Advisory test gate: CONCERNS
findings.evidence: P0 pinned: no_em_dash_in_any_template_test, no_reply_stop_anywhere_test, invite_sms_carries_form_notice_and_stop_links_test, send_invite_no_keys_skips_both_channels_test, email_outcome_maps_ok_to_delivered_with_id_test. P1 gap: AC3 email sender/tag wiring uncovered.
findings.detail: P0 100% (Art 14 block, stop-link in every SMS, no reply-STOP, no-op-without-keys, outcome mapping, em-dash ban all pinned). P1 ~88%, overall ~93%: the AC3 email seam is the single P1 gap.
findings.recommended_fix: Pin the sender/tag seam and add the empty-detail attempt-line test; that lifts P1 to 100% and the gate to PASS.

findings.title: Warm-handoff count line says "tried to reach them" where the spec pinned "messaged them" (disclosed in the dev record, spec not amended)
findings.evidence: "We've tried to reach them " vs spec pin: "We've messaged them {attempt_count} times over the last 4 days. The attempt log:"
findings.detail: Disclosed in the dev record's spec-to-implementation deltas with a rationale (truthful when the log includes the applicant co-nudge), so review-visible — but the spec's pinned copy was not updated.
findings.recommended_fix: Accept the disclosed delta and update the spec's pinned copy, or revert the string.

findings.title: Greeting-split capitalisation in reminder-1 and co-nudge deviates from pinned copy but is documented only for reminder-2
findings.evidence: Pinned: "Hi {referee_first_name}, a quick reminder about the reference form for ..." / "Hi {applicant_first_name}, we've invited ..."; implemented as separate paragraphs: "Hi " <> name <> "," <> email_paragraph("A quick reminder about ...") / "We've invited ..."
findings.detail: The greeting becomes its own paragraph and the next sentence capitalises in reminder-1 and co-nudge too; the dev record documents this reconciliation only for reminder-2.
findings.recommended_fix: Add the greeting-split to the spec's documented deviations for all affected templates.

findings.title: Unresolved '??' placeholder shipped in send.gleam doc comment and spec T4.2
findings.evidence: "the sweep applies corrected ?? snapshot before calling — AD-7's effective-contact rule lives with the caller" (send.gleam doc) / "(the sweep resolves corrected ?? snapshot before calling)" (spec T4.2)
findings.detail: 'corrected ?? snapshot' is an undecided placeholder, not prose; it ships in the module doc rc3-5's implementer reads. The repo bans placeholders in code and docs.
findings.recommended_fix: Replace '??' with the intended wording (e.g. the actual AD-7 rule name) in both files.

findings.title: first_name's [] branch is unreachable (string.split always yields at least one element)
findings.detail: split of an empty (trimmed) string yields [""], so [first, ..] always matches and the [] arm is dead; if it ever fired it would return the untrimmed raw name, contradicting the documented '' behaviour.
findings.recommended_fix: Drop the unreachable [] arm and handle the empty case explicitly.

findings.title: first_name exported with no production caller (rc3-5 is the intended consumer)
findings.evidence: pub fn first_name(name name: String) -> String { ... } — only server/test/reference_checks/messages_test.gleam calls it; no src/ caller.
findings.detail: Public API committed ahead of its consumer. Acceptable if rc3-5 lands next; worth a doc-comment note naming the sweep as the caller.
findings.recommended_fix: Name the sweep as the caller in the doc comment, or defer the helper to rc3-5.

findings.title: Empty attempt log renders "We've tried to reach them 0 times over the last 4 days" (spec-pinned shape, awkward when 0)
findings.evidence: "We've tried to reach them " <> count <> " times over the last 4 days. The attempt log:" with test pinning "No attempts recorded." and "0 times"
findings.detail: The count paragraph renders unconditionally; with attempts = [] a landlord sees '0 times' plus 'No attempts recorded.'. The pinned copy authored this shape, so it is a copy-deck question, not an implementation bug.
findings.recommended_fix: When attempts is [], omit the count paragraph (keep only the honest empty state); update the pinned copy and test.

findings.title: item_style hardcodes the brand font stack instead of composing brand_font
findings.evidence:
const brand_font = "'DM Sans', -apple-system, BlinkMacSystemFont, 'Segoe UI', Roboto, sans-serif"

const item_style = "font-family: 'DM Sans', -apple-system, BlinkMacSystemFont, 'Segoe UI', Roboto, sans-serif; font-size: 15px; ..."
findings.detail: The same font stack is duplicated verbatim one line below the const that exists to hold it; a brand-font change would silently drift the attempt-log <li> styling.
findings.recommended_fix: Compose item_style from brand_font like email_paragraph/notice_footer do.

findings.title: Email markup primitives + brand tokens now duplicated in two modules (deliberate per spec decision 7)
findings.evidence: messages.gleam const brand_font duplicates email_client.gleam:1245 const brand_font; fn email_wrapper/cta_button/email_divider/fallback_link mirror the private fns at email_client.gleam:1283/1342/1355/1359 incl. brand colors #1B2A4A/#D4942A.
findings.detail: Deliberate per decision 7 (extraction deferred until a third email family), so not a defect — but brand font/colors are now two-source; a rebrand must edit both modules or emails drift visually.
findings.recommended_fix: No change now; extract a shared email_markup module when the next email family or rebrand lands, per the spec's own trigger.

findings.title: Warm-handoff attempt-line empty-detail branch unpinned (both fixtures carry non-empty detail)
findings.evidence: case entry.detail { "" -> "" detail -> " (" <> email_client.escape_html(detail) <> ")" } — fixtures only use detail: "resend-id-1" and detail: "Twilio API error: HTTP 400".
findings.detail: P3 render branch: a delivered/skipped attempt with no provider id renders without the parenthesised suffix; that output shape is untested.
findings.recommended_fix: Add an AttemptEntry with detail: "" and assert the line renders as `at: channel, outcome` with no trailing parenthesis.
